findings.issue_text: Google Calendar: refreshOAuthTokens returns fetch Response instead of GaxiosResponse when credential sharing is enabled, causing res.data to be undefined and throwing TypeError on token access

Hubspot: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response instead of HubspotToken when credential sharing is on, causing .access_token, .refresh_token, and .expires_in to be undefined and storing garbage tokens
Zoho Bigin: refreshOAuthTokens passes credentialId instead of credential.userId as the third argument, preventing correct user credential lookup when credential sharing is enabled

Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM: refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response instead of AxiosResponse when credential sharing is enabled, causing .data to be undefined and throwing TypeError on access to .data.error or .data.expiryDate

Office365: parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites the real refresh_token with the literal sentinel string "refresh_token" when refresh_token is absent, corrupting persisted credentials and permanently breaking future token refreshes
Salesforce: error detection uses response.statusText !== "OK" instead of response.ok, which is unreliable with HTTP/2 and can cause valid responses to throw or invalid ones to pass

parseRefreshTokenResponse minimumTokenResponseSchema uses broken computed keys [z.string().toString()] which both resolve to "[object Object]", failing to validate an expiry field or meaningfully allow arbitrary properties
app-credential.ts webhook uses z.parse() which throws an unhandled ZodError on malformed request body, resulting in a raw 500 error instead of a clean 400 validation response
Broken Zod schema bypasses token validation when credential sharing is enabled because computed keys evaluate to '[object Object]', stripping required fields
Unhandled decryption/JSON-parse errors in the credential webhook due to missing try/catch around symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse
Non-constant-time comparison of webhook secret using !== leaks timing information about the secret
External HTTP call in refreshOAuthTokens.ts has no timeout, no error handling, and no retry/backoff, risking indefinite blocking of calendar operations under sync
Four sequential DB roundtrips per webhook call in app-credential.ts with no parallelization of independent lookups
Broken Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: z.string().toString() resolves to literal key '[object Object]', weakening validation to near no-op
Return-type mismatch in refreshOAuthTokens.ts: sync-enabled branch returns raw fetch Response object, but callers expect parsed/typed result, causing TypeError on every refresh

Zod schema in `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` which evaluate to `[object Object]`, creating a no-op schema that bypasses caller strict schemas when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, leading to malformed tokens being persisted and breaking future OAuth refreshes

`refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns a raw fetch `Response` when the sync endpoint is configured, but callers (Hubspot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin) expect an Axios response with `.data` or a parsed object, causing undefined access and contract breaks

`app-credential.ts:55` uses `z.parse(req.body)` which throws an unhandled ZodError producing a 500 instead of a 4xx for malformed request bodies
`app-credential.ts:60-63` webhook secret comparison uses `!==` instead of a constant-time comparison, making it vulnerable to timing attacks
`app-credential.ts` has no HTTP method restriction, accepting any method (GET, etc.) when webhook convention is POST-only
`app-credential.ts:67-69` leaves `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` unguarded, so malformed ciphertext or misconfigured AES keys throw a 500 with potential info leakage

`zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` hardcodes redirect URI `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` instead of using `appConfig.slug`, potentially breaking OAuth install if the registered Zoho redirect uses a different slug

`parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:18-20` mutates `refreshTokenResponse.data` to add `refresh_token` after `safeParse`, but the Zod schema output type doesn't declare `refresh_token`, causing TypeScript errors for downstream typed callers

`CalendarService.ts:79-93` performs token refresh unconditionally on every `SalesforceCalendarService` construction, changing the persisted credential key shape and potentially breaking other code paths that read the original shape
minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to literal strings, making the schema nonsense and failing validation

Salesforce checks response.statusText !== "OK", rejecting valid 200 responses with different statusText

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app-credential.ts webhook uses z.parse() which throws an unhandled ZodError on malformed request body, resulting in a raw 500 error instead of a clean 400 validation response
Broken Zod schema bypasses token validation when credential sharing is enabled because computed keys evaluate to '[object Object]', stripping required fields

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed keys are evaluated immediately to a single string (very likely `"[object Object]"` or similar), not a pattern matching “any numeric expiry field”. This makes the schema effectively only enforce `access_token` (and possibly a single weirdly-named property), so when credential sharing is enabled it weakens/bypasses the intended token validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled decryption/JSON-parse errors in the credential webhook due to missing try/catch around symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse
Non-constant-time comparison of webhook secret using !== leaks timing information about the secret

adjudication.rationale:
In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret check is implemented as a direct string comparison:

```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```

JavaScript/Node string equality (`!==`) is not guaranteed to be constant-time and may short-circuit on the first differing character/length, which can leak timing information about `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to a remote caller who can repeatedly probe the endpoint and measure response times. A constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` with normalized buffers) is the standard mitigation for comparing secrets used for authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External HTTP call in refreshOAuthTokens.ts has no timeout, no error handling, and no retry/backoff, risking indefinite blocking of calendar operations under sync

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, which performs an external `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` with no AbortController/timeout and no handling of non-2xx responses (it returns the raw `Response` without checking `ok`). Node/undici `fetch` has no default timeout, so this can hang until the runtime/network times out, potentially blocking token refresh/calendar operations when sync is enabled. There is also no retry/backoff in this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Four sequential DB roundtrips per webhook call in app-credential.ts with no parallelization of independent lookups

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does multiple Prisma calls in sequence: `user.findUnique`, `app.findUnique`, `credential.findFirst`, then either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. That is indeed 4 DB operations per request in the success path, and the user/app lookups are independent so they could be parallelized. However, this is a performance optimization suggestion rather than a clear bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff; the code is functionally correct as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts: z.string().toString() resolves to literal key '[object Object]', weakening validation to near no-op

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is declared as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In JS, computed property keys must be a `string | symbol`; here `z.string()` is a Zod object and `.toString()` will yield a literal key like `"[object Object]"`, not an “any string key”/index signature. So the schema does **not** validate “any numeric expiry field” or “allow other properties” as intended; it just defines (and likely overwrites) a single literal key, weakening validation.

`refreshOAuthTokens.ts` returns a raw fetch `Response` when the sync endpoint is configured, but callers (Hubspot, Zoho CRM, Zoho Bigin) expect an Axios response with `.data` or a parsed object, causing undefined access and contract breaks

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` when syncing is enabled, i.e. a raw `Response`. At least one caller in the diff expects an object/axios-like response: in `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` it does `const token = res?.data;` after calling `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined`, and subsequent `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date` will fail at runtime. Similarly, `hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts` types the return as `HubspotToken`, but under syncing it would instead get a `Response`, breaking the expected contract (even though it's not specifically axios there). The mention of Zoho callers isn't verifiable from this diff, but the core contract-break issue is present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` never checks `response.ok` or error status, allowing 4xx/5xx responses from the sync endpoint to be silently parsed as JSON and persisted unvalidated

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` does not check `response.ok`, but it also does not parse JSON or persist anything itself—it just returns whatever `fetch`/`refreshFunction` returns. In the diff, some callers (e.g., Office365) pass the returned `Response` into `handleErrorsJson(...)`, which by its name is likely where HTTP error handling happens (not verifiable here, but the diff doesn’t show silent parsing). Other callers (e.g., GoogleCalendar) treat the return as an object with `.data`, which would fail loudly if the sync endpoint returns a `fetch` `Response` or a 4xx/5xx, rather than “silently parsed and persisted.” Therefore the specific claim about silently parsing 4xx/5xx JSON and persisting it unvalidated is not directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `CalendarService.ts:84` uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` as a success check, which is unreliable because HTTP/2 forbids reason phrases and servers may return empty statusText for 2xx responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show any code using `response.statusText !== "OK"` as a success check in any `CalendarService.ts` snippet shown (Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office365). The updated logic uses `handleErrorsJson`, `handleLarkError`, or reads `res.data` directly, and the new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper returns a `Response` without checking `statusText`. Therefore the finding cites a condition that is not present/verifiable in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app-credential.ts:55` uses `z.parse(req.body)` which throws an unhandled ZodError producing a 500 instead of a 4xx for malformed request bodies

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body);` without a surrounding `try/catch` or using `safeParse`. `zod.parse` throws a `ZodError` on malformed input, and in a Next.js API route an uncaught exception will result in a 500 response. So malformed request bodies would produce a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx (typically 400).

adjudication_records.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys that evaluate to literal strings, making the schema nonsense and failing validation

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Here `z.string()` returns a ZodString object, and calling `.toString()` on it yields a literal string (e.g. "[object Object]"), not a dynamic/pattern key. This makes the schema effectively require a numeric property with that literal name (and the second computed key likely overwrites the first because it resolves to the same string), so typical OAuth token responses like `{ access_token, expiry_date, refresh_token }` will not satisfy the schema and `safeParse` will fail.
